newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Deutsche Telekom booms in debut.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Deutsche Telekom booms in debut.

text.p: Germany's state telephone company Deutsche Telekom made a stellar debut as an American Depositary Receipt (ADR) on Monday, rising 2-47/64 to 21-5/8 in heavy trade.

The stock, part of a $13 billion global share offering in the company's first stage of privatization, eased from a high of 22-1/8 reached just minutes after opening. Volume was 12.6 million shares, by far the most active stock on Wall Street.
Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading for Schroder Wertheim, noted traders had seen gains of $3 to $4 a share on overnight purchases of the stock.
"They are just saying, 'Hey, thank you very much," and moving on to the next thing," he said. "You're going to see very active trading for some time to come."
Among other European ADRs, British Gas Plc rose 3-5/8 to 38-1/2 on a report in London's Sunday Telegraph that Royal Dutch/Shell Group had approached the company with merger proposals.

Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc rose one to 99-3/4 and Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was up 3-1/4 to 170-5/8, a record for its ADR. Oil stocks generally also have benefited in recent weeks from rising oil prices.
Among Latin American stocks, Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile, or Soquimich fell 2-5/8 to 55 after Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said it was downgrading its rating for the company to sell from buy.
Decliners led advancers by 277-224 among an 807-ADR index. Volume at midday was 31.8 million shares.
